## Paper

Multi-Agent Actor-Critic for Mixed Cooperative-Competitive Environments

## World

cross_world_methods

## Institution

Not applicable: method paper.

## Agent type

Centralized-training/decentralized-execution actor-critic MARL.

## Theoretical benchmark

MARL benchmark: decentralized actors with a critic that can condition on broader joint or centralized information during training.

## Learning setup

Actor policies act from local observations; the critic/value estimate uses centralized context where available; evaluation distinguishes centralized training from decentralized execution.

## Metrics

World-level welfare/stability/exploitability plus comparison against DQN, PPO, and independent-DQN; special attention to asymmetric-agent worlds.

## Main result

The paper demonstrates that multi-agent actor-critic methods can successfully learn complex coordination strategies in both cooperative and competitive environments, outperforming traditional methods like DQN and DDPG.

## What they prove

The paper motivates and empirically evaluates centralized-training/decentralized-execution actor-critic methods for mixed cooperative-competitive settings. Use it as a method-design obligation, not as a formal proof of convergence or effectiveness in all multi-agent environments.

## What they only simulate

Empirical performance in benchmark multi-agent environments.

## What they do NOT test

The paper does not test the method on real-world economic systems or provide formal guarantees on the robustness of the learned policies.

## What we need to reproduce

Reproduce the interface-level obligation: centralized critic must be structurally distinct from independent learners, handle fixed observation dimensions, and either support or explicitly reject asymmetric-agent worlds. Evidence: minds/marl/centralized_critic.py; cross-world P.6 smoke/full outputs..

## How our project differs

The paper studies mixed cooperative-competitive MARL. This repo adapts the pattern to economic worlds; Labor Market asymmetry is a real stress test rather than a minor config change.

## Implementation obligations

Decentralized actor action selection; centralized value/critic input when configured; consistent obs_dim/action_dim handling; no accidental fallback to independent DQN; explicit validation in symmetric and asymmetric worlds.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

minds/marl/centralized_critic.py; cross-world P.6 smoke/full outputs; synthesis tables separating centralized-critic from independent-DQN.

## Failure modes to audit

Centralized critic implemented as a label around independent learners; critic sees inconsistent dimensions; asymmetric agents forced through a symmetric interface; smoke validation without full-run interpretation.
